transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-11-05
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Jared Patel (Head of ML, Medivex), Sana Mir (PM), Luis Ortega (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Short: Team reviewed recent quality regressions on the billing-intent prompt set; agreed to update prompt annotations, run a dedicated perf benchmark, and have a security follow-up on KMS/HSM.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we have about 40 minutes. Quick around the room?
[00:06] Jared Patel: Hey, Jared here, head of ML at Medivex. We'll share the failure set after.
[00:10] Sana Mir: Sana, product. I'm focused on accuracy for triage flow and minimizing false positives.
[00:14] Luis Ortega: Luis, security. I'll mainly be listening for KMS and data residency notes.
[00:18] Devon Park: Devon from Redwood, I'll run through the eval diffs and perf asks.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Cool, agenda: results recap from last week, deep-dive on the billing-intent regressions, proposed prompt adjustments, scoring thresholds, guardrails, then next steps.

[02:05] Devon Park: Ok so quick snapshot; we re-run the eval against the 2k prompt set — overall intent accuracy dropped from about 92% pre-patch to 85% post-patch on the billing-intent slice, most of the diffs were around the multi-step utterances. Some of these look like prompt framing sensitivity.
[02:29] Jared Patel: That's... higher impact than we expected. Are these from the new quantized model?
[02:33] Devon Park: Good question. We tested both the quantized float16 path and our int8-ish quant variant — there's a small delta but the main regression appears even on FP32. So it's more prompt-sensitive than pure quantization.

[05:10] Sana Mir: Can you show an example? A couple of customer tickets were flagged as incorrect.
[05:15] Devon Park: Sure, example: user says, "I need to dispute a charge on my Oct bill; can you tell me how?" The model responded with a generic refund flow instead of triage to 'billing-dispute' route. In some cases it hallucinated a policy link.
[05:36] Maya Chen: Hallucination + intent misclass — we need guardrails. We recommended retrieval augmentation last week; did retrieval reduce hallucinations here?
[05:42] Devon Park: Retrieval helped on content accuracy but didn't fully fix the intent label mapping. The mapping to your downstream router is fuzzy when the prompt has multiple clauses.

[08:00] Jared Patel: So is this a prompt rewrite issue? We had some templated prompts that were changed for brevity. Maybe the shorthand created ambiguity.
[08:09] Devon Park: Exactly. We looked at three variants: verbose template, short template, and context-window template that includes last 2 user messages. The verbose one is most robust but raises token cost ~12%. The context-window helps but sometimes misses the 'dispute' intent when embedded in a compound sentence.

[11:12] Maya Chen: On scoring — how are you currently scoring pass/fail? We use a combination right? Precision on intent mapping and human rating for answer correctness?
[11:20] Devon Park: Yep — pipeline is automated: string-based intent match + semantic similarity score threshold (embedding cosine >= 0.78) + a human verification sample. For the report I included precision/recall numbers and a human-accept rate. We also have a 'soft-fail' bucket that triggers fallback to human or reroute to a form.
[11:44] Sana Mir: That 0.78 threshold feels brittle. Can we A/B thresholds?
[11:48] Devon Park: Absolutely — we can sweep thresholds. Suggest we try 0.75/0.78/0.82 and run the 2k set to see tradeoffs for false positives vs false negatives.

[15:05] Maya Chen: Guardrails: aside from retrieval, we talked about regex and entity-check. Any progress?
[15:12] Devon Park: We prototyped a pre-check: simple regex for invoice numbers and keywords like 'dispute', 'charge', 'overcharged'. If regex triggers, we bias prompt with a directive "Prioritize routing to billing-dispute" using system role. That reduces some misses but isn't perfect for paraphrase.
[15:36] Luis Ortega: From security side, we want to ensure no PHI is sent to the hosted model. Our data retention policy requires redaction at source. Are you comfortable with redaction hooks?
[15:46] Devon Park: Yes — Redwood supports client-side redaction; we also have optional private deployment (VPC) and key management integrations for Private customers. We can share SOC2 and KMS docs.
[16:05] Luis Ortega: Okay, we'll need the compliance pack and a short doc on KMS/HSM flow. Also, are logs redactable before leaving your control plane?
[16:14] Maya Chen: Logs can be filtered and we offer token-level retention controls; we can deliver the compliance checklist to you. We'll add that as an action item.

[18:30] Jared Patel: Back to quality — you mentioned some models earlier had smaller deltas. Which model variants were in the test?
[18:36] Devon Park: We tested Redwood-curated-open-1 (baseline), rwd-opt-1-qlf (quant-lite), and a tuned checkpoint with instruction-tuning for customer samples. The tuned checkpoint did better on short prompts but slightly worse on compound sentences. It seems the tuning traded off robustness for conciseness.

[21:00] Sana Mir: Could we do hybrid: keep tuned checkpoint for short FAQs, route compound utterances to baseline?
[21:08] Devon Park: Yes, smart routing policy can do that — route by predicted length or complexity score. That's something Redwood's routing layer supports; we can set canary percentages.

[24:05] Maya Chen: Perf question — you asked to run a dedicated perf run last week. Any results?
[24:12] Devon Park: We're scheduling a 2-hour bench on a dedicated 4-GPU pool (similar to your Dedicated sizing). Early numbers show median token latency around 45ms per-token on baseline with batching at your expected qps,  tail 95 at ~120ms. When enabling KV caching and prefix caching we get better user-perceived latency for multi-turn flows. I'll attach raw logs.
[24:40] Jared Patel: Cost implications?
[24:43] Devon Park: Hosted is cheaper short-term; Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost at scale but requires a commit. We'll include a cost-per-1M tokens calc for the two paths — tradeoff is latency predictability and data isolation.

[28:20] Sana Mir: For eval scoring, can we add a human-in-the-loop quick pass for the 200 highest-impact examples?
[28:26] Devon Park: Yep, we can flag by confidence score and surface to your team via the console. We also support an export CSV for labeling.

[31:55] Luis Ortega: Quick security note — if we go Dedicated, how's KMS integrated? Are keys customer-managed?
[32:02] Devon Park: In Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM (bring your own key). For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but can integrate with AWS KMS via cross-account role. We'll send the keyflow diagram.

[34:10] Maya Chen: Ok let's lock concrete next steps — prompt updates, threshold sweeps, perf bench and security doc.
[34:20] Devon Park: Proposed timeline: prompt re-annotations by 11/07, threshold sweep 11/10, perf run results 11/10, security call 11/12.
[34:32] Jared Patel: Works for us. Also we'll prioritize sending the 50 worst failure examples by Friday.

[36:40] Maya Chen: Any blockers we didn't cover?
[36:44] Sana Mir: None from product; just need the eval spreadsheet format.
[36:48] Luis Ortega: Please include a short NDA/POC data flow in the compliance pack.
[36:53] Maya Chen: Will do.

[39:00] Devon Park: I'll attach the eval diffs CSV and a sample of the prompted variants in the follow-up email.
[39:06] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with updated artifacts.
[39:12] Jared Patel: Thanks all.
[39:15] Sana Mir: Thanks.
[39:18] Luis Ortega: Bye.
